questions_and_answers.question: A nurse provides medication instructions to a first-time mother. Which statement made by the mother indicates a need for further instructions? A. "I should mix the medication in the baby food and give it when I feed the child" B. "I should administer the oral medication sitting in an upright position and with the head elevated" C. "I will give my child a toy after giving the medication" D. "I will offer my child a juice drink after swallowing the medication"
questions_and_answers.answer: A. "I should mix the medication in the baby food and give it to my child" The nurse would teach the mother to avoid putting medications in foods because it may cause an unpleasant taste to the food, and the child may refuse to accept the same food in the future. Additionally the child may not consume the entire dosage. B. Administering the medication in an upright position and head elevated will prevent the risk of aspiration. C. Offering a toy will provide comfort measures to the child. D. The mother should offer drink such as juice or a soft drink to lessen the aftertaste of the medication.

questions_and_answers.question: 3-A nurse provides medication instructions to a first-time mother.Which statement made by the mother indicates a need for further instructions? Select one: a. "I should administer the oral medication sitting in an upright position and with the head elevated". b."I will offer my child a juice drink after swallowing the medication". c. "I will give my child a toy after giving the medication". d."I should mix the medication in the baby food and give it when I feed the child".
questions_and_answers.answer: Option D.. The question focuses on proper medication administration for infants, which is crucial for ensuring safety and effectiveness. The correct answer will highlight a misunderstanding or a potentially harmful practice regarding how to administer medication to a child. Here are further explanations. - **Option A**: This statement is correct as administering oral medication while sitting upright and with the head elevated is a safe practice to prevent choking and ensure proper swallowing. - **Option B**: This option is also appropriate because offering a juice drink after medication can help wash down the medicine and make it more palatable for the child. - **Option C**: This statement is acceptable as giving a toy as a reward after taking medication can help encourage compliance in children. - **Option D**: This option raises concern because mixing medication with baby food can lead to inaccurate dosing. If the child does not finish the food, they may not receive the full dose of medication, which could be dangerous.
